predecessors.note: Cliopatria has no Mtetwa row; extent unknown.

successors.note: Cliopatria's Natalia Republic row (1840-1910) is the Colony of Natal.

capitals.name: kwaBulawayo
capitals.note: Infobox lists the capitals without years; years from the reigns of Shaka (1816-1828), Dingane (1828-1840), Mpande (1840-1856); coordinates are the researcher's and approximate.

capitals.name: Ulundi
capitals.note: Ulundi from the gazetteer. Cetshwayo's kraal at Ulundi was attacked on 22 July 1883 (Anglo-Zulu War page).

rulers.name: Cetshwayo
rulers.note: Captured 28 August 1879, restored in 1883, died February 1884.

correction.text: the Zulu core between the Tugela and the Pongola, as Cliopatria's 1820 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1816-1819 (Cliopatria's row starts in 1820): the infobox 'Founding: Shaka's accession, 1816'. The page gives no extent before the Mhlatuze River victory of 1820 (Shaka was subordinate to the Mtetwa Paramountcy); Cliopatria's 1820 shape is used as the bridge (unverified).

1820-1839, 25,596 km2. The infobox gives 207,000 km2 for 1822 (ratio 0.12) and the text 'an empire covering an area of around 80,000 square miles (210,000 km2)' reaching from the Pongola to the Tugela; but the land between those two rivers is some 26,000 km2, so the page's figure is for a sphere of conquest and tribute, not for the land held. The shape is kept as the direct kingdom; the wider sphere is not drawn because the page names no lands.
1840-1847, 25,623 km2, Mpande's first years. The Boer republic of Natalia lay south of the Tugela from 1839; Cliopatria's Natalia row starts in 1840.

1856-1884, 25,464 km2. Holds to 1883 for the pages opened. After the British invasion of January 1879 the kingdom was divided 'into thirteen chiefdoms headed by compliant chiefs' (undated) and Cetshwayo was restored in 1883 'over a buffer reserve territory, much reduced from his original kingdom'; neither page gives boundaries, so the full shape stands unverified for 1879-1884. In August 1884 the north-west goes to the New Republic (ledger).

minus.text: the north-west of Zululand granted to the Boers in 1884 (1,355,000 morgen; the republic's area 13,600 km2 gives the radius), capital Vryheid

keyframe_review.note: 1885-1894, 25,013 km2. The Nieuwe Republiek (5 or 16 August 1884 to 20 July 1888, capital Vryheid, area 13,600 km2) took in, initially, the whole northwest of Zululand (page's words, not a quotation). Cliopatria's Zululand shape still contains the Vryheid country (8 of the 18 cells within 40 km of Vryheid) while its own Nieuwe Republiek shape (10,205 km2) lies at lon 31.8-32.7, far from Vryheid, so the republic's row looks misplaced. The north-west is removed here. Britain annexed Zululand in 1887 and the Republic joined the Transvaal in 1888.

minus.text: the north-west of Zululand granted to the Boers in 1884 (1,355,000 morgen; the republic's area 13,600 km2 gives the radius), capital Vryheid

correction.text: Zululand without the former New Republic land, which the Transvaal had absorbed in 1888

keyframe_review.note: 1895-1897, 24,962 km2: the same, without the north-west. Zululand was annexed to Natal in 1897 ('Annexed Zululand: 1897', the Colony of Natal infobox).

region.text: the Zulu core, as Cliopatria's 1820 shape

ledger.note: 1816: Shaka comes to power and founds the Zulu kingdom. The infobox gives 'Founding: Shaka's accession, 1816' and the Mtetwa Paramountcy as predecessor; the battle of Gqokli Hill (1818) is listed as a milestone. The page gives no extent for 1816.

region.text: the country from the Pongola to the Tugela

ledger.note: 1820: Shaka breaks the Ndwandwe. The page has him defeat Zwide at the Battle of Mhlatuze River in 1820, breaking up the Ndwandwe alliance, after surviving Zwide's first assault at Gqokli Hill (1818); 'By 1822, Shaka had conquered an empire' from the Pongola to the Tugela. Cliopatria's shape begins in 1820.

1828: the capital moves from kwaBulawayo to uMgungundlovu with Dingane. The infobox lists kwaBulawayo, uMgungundlovu and Ulundi without years; the order and the reigns (Shaka 1816-1828, Dingane 1828-1840) give the dates (page silent).

region.text: the land south of the Tugela River

ledger.note: 3-4 February 1838: Dingane cedes the land south of the Tugela to the Voortrekkers. 'a treaty was signed, wherein Dingane ceded all the land south of the Tugela River' (Piet Retief's visit, October 1837); the Boers defeated the Zulus at Blood River on 16 December 1838 and formed Natalia in 1839. The shape never held the land south of the Tugela, so this changes no drawn cells.
1840: the capital moves to Ulundi with Mpande (infobox: kwaBulawayo, uMgungundlovu, Ulundi; no years given; the reign years are Mpande 1840-1856).

region.text: Zululand, invaded from Natal and the Transvaal border

ledger.note: 11 January 1879: British forces invade Zululand. 'On 11 January, they crossed the border and invaded Zululand' (ultimatum of 11 December 1878 to Cetshwayo); Isandlwana on 22 January.

4 July 1879: the Battle of Ulundi ends the war. 'On 4 July, the armies clashed at the Battle of Ulundi, and Cetshwayo's forces were decisively defeated'; the king was captured on 28 August 1879 and, undated on the page, Zululand was divided 'into thirteen chiefdoms headed by compliant chiefs'.

region.text: the north-west of Zululand granted to the Boers in 1884 (1,355,000 morgen; the republic's area 13,600 km2 gives the radius), capital Vryheid

ledger.note: 16 August 1884: Dinuzulu grants the north-west to the Boers. After the Boers and Dinuzulu's Usuthu defeated Zibhebhu (5 June 1884, Tshaneni) 'Dinuzulu issued a proclamation granting 1 355 000 morgen' for a republic, formed on 5 August 1884; the whole northwest of Zululand, with its border extended to the sea between the Mhlatuze River and St Lucia Bay (the page's wording). The radius round Vryheid is the researcher's reading of the republic's 13,600 km2.

1887: Britain annexes Zululand. 'The British Empire made the Zulu Kingdom a protectorate and later annexed it in 1887'; the Zulu Kingdom infobox: 'Protectorate of the United Kingdom, 1887-1897'. Dinuzulu's reign ends in 1887. Colour and dossier continue.

1897: Zululand is annexed to Natal. 'John Robinson remained premier until 1897, a year marked by the annexation of Zululand to Natal' (infobox 'Annexed Zululand: 1897'); the Zulu Kingdom infobox 'to Natal: 1897'. Cliopatria's Natal row is natalia-republic.

wars.name: Shaka's wars against the Ndwandwe
wars.outcome: Zwide's first assault failed at Gqokli Hill (1818); Shaka defeated him at the Mhlatuze River in 1820, breaking the Ndwandwe alliance.
wars.note: Empty zones: the page names the rivers but no ground that changed hands.

wars.name: Zulu-Voortrekker war and the Battle of Blood River

zones.text: the land south of the Tugela River

wars.outcome: Dingane ceded the land south of the Tugela (February 1838); Pretorius's forces held at Blood River on 16 December 1838; the Boers formed Natalia 'south of the Tugela' in 1839.

wars.name: Zulu invasion of Swaziland
wars.outcome: Mpande invaded Swaziland in 1852 and the British pressured him to withdraw.

wars.name: Anglo-Zulu War
wars.outcome: British victory at Ulundi (4 July 1879) after Isandlwana (22 January); Cetshwayo captured on 28 August and the kingdom divided into thirteen chiefdoms.

wars.name: Zulu Civil War (Usuthu against Zibhebhu)

zones.text: the north-west of Zululand granted to the Boers in 1884 (1,355,000 morgen; the republic's area 13,600 km2 gives the radius), capital Vryheid

wars.outcome: Zibhebhu attacked Cetshwayo's kraal at Ulundi on 22 July 1883; the Boers and Dinuzulu defeated him at Tshaneni on 5 June 1884; the Boers received the north-west.
wars.note: The Anglo-Zulu War page gives the 1883 attack; the Nieuwe Republiek page the 1884 battle.

certainty.note: The Pongola and Tugela rivers are the only lines the page names; nothing was surveyed.
The thirteen chiefdoms (1879), the 1883 reserve and the 1884 grant of 1,355,000 morgen have no boundaries on the pages.

sources.note: Identity, infobox 207,000 km2 (1822), rulers, Mhlatuze 1820, Blood River 1838, Natalia 1839, the war of 1879, 1883-1884, 1887, 1897.

sources.title: Zululand

sources.title: Anglo-Zulu War
sources.note: Invasion 11 January 1879, Ulundi 4 July, Cetshwayo captured 28 August, thirteen chiefdoms (undated), restoration 1883, protectorate and annexation 1887.

sources.title: Nieuwe Republiek
sources.note: The New Republic of 1884-1888: Tshaneni 5 June 1884, formed 5 August, 1,355,000 morgen on 16 August, recognised 22 October 1886, 13,600 km2, joined the Transvaal 20 July 1888.

sources.title: Colony of Natal
sources.note: Zululand annexed to Natal in 1897; Natal proclaimed a colony on 4 May 1843; the Tugela and Buffalo as Natal's boundary.

notes:
Cliopatria's Wikipedia field for this row is 'Zululand', which is a disambiguation page (Zulu Kingdom 1818-1897 and the KwaZulu bantustan); the dossier is titled 'Zulu Kingdom' and cites that article. Wikidata Q13558877 is Cliopatria's.

Infobox area: 207,000 km2 in 1822 against Cliopatria's 25,596 km2: the shape is kept (see the 1820 verdict); the page's 'Pongola to the Tugela' limits are about 26,000 km2. Shaka's wider sphere (the Mthethwa and Ndwandwe lands, Natal) and tributary relations are not drawn: no page opened names lands or dates them. The loss of the land south of the Tugela (February 1838) is a claim, not in the shape.

Not settled: the extent of Shaka's kingdom in 1816-1819; the thirteen chiefdoms of 1879 and the reduced reserve of 1883 (no boundaries, no month); the pre-1879 changes of Cliopatria's 1840/1848/1856 cells (a few cells at the Natal border); Mpande's cession 'between the Buffalo and Tugela' to Natal (undated on the Colony of Natal page); the Utrecht district and the 'Disputed Territory' (not on any page opened). Cliopatria's Nieuwe Republiek shape (lon 31.8-32.7) does not contain Vryheid (30.8 E); the af-07-b dossier must settle it. The 1887 British protectorate / Crown territory is only one line on the pages. The Zulu Kingdom page dates the British annexation of Natalia 1842, the Colony of Natal page proclaims Natal a colony on 4 May 1843.

Counterparts needing dossiers: Mtetwa Paramountcy, Ndwandwe Kingdom (both predecessors in the Zulu rise), Swazi kingdom before 1885, Zibhebhu's Mandlakazi chiefdom; natalia-republic, nieuwe-republiek, british-colonial-empire exist as Cliopatria rows.
